newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate dips to 10.7 pct from 11.9.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate dips to 10.7 pct from 11.9.

text.p: The Croatian average lending rate fell to 10.7 percent on Monday from 11.9 percent as the supply of kuna funds outstripped demand in slower trading.
Settlements totalled 31.7 million kuna, leaving a surplus of 10 million kuna on the supply side.
Fresh borrowings acccounted for 22.7 million kuna, mostly made at a steady call money rate of 10.5 percent.
Insurers extended old loans at nine percent while banks rolled over previous term loans at 16 percent and call money borrowings at 10.5 percent.
The central bank calculated its kuna mid-rates for Tuesday firmer at 5.9842 against the dollar and weaker at 3.5716 against the German mark. -- Zoran Radosavljevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
